claim_text: bowel cancer screening from 50 (earlier with a family history)
old_wording: bowel screening from 50 (earlier with a family history)
new_wording: bowel cancer screening (the national program covers ages 45 to 74); a family history or symptoms may mean earlier or different checks rather than routine screening. Also updated the 40s and 50s FAQs from 'from 50' to reflect ages 45 to 74.

primary_source.org: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing
primary_source.title: National Bowel Cancer Screening Program - lowered eligible age

evidence_summary: The National Bowel Cancer Screening Program eligibility is now 45-74, free iFOBT every 2 years. Ages 50-74 are automatically invited; 45-49 can request their first kit. 'From 50' is outdated.
limitations: Population screening applies to people without symptoms. Symptoms or a significant family history warrant assessment/colonoscopy pathways, not the routine screening test - the revised copy separates these.
reviewer_notes: Verified this turn via WebSearch of health.gov.au and Cancer Council. Independently corroborated by the MID audit agent (MID-13, MID-16). Screening ages change - short review cycle.

claim_text: Often cholesterol and other lipids, blood glucose or HbA1c, kidney and liver function, and iron studies, with others added depending on your history and symptoms.
old_wording: Often cholesterol and other lipids, blood glucose or HbA1c, kidney and liver function, and iron studies (to check for low iron), with others added depending on your history and symptoms.
new_wording: It depends on your age, history and risk factors. Commonly considered are cholesterol and other lipids and blood glucose or HbA1c (for cardiovascular and diabetes risk), with selected tests such as kidney function, liver function or iron studies where they're clinically useful.

primary_source.title: Guidelines for preventive activities in general practice (Red Book)

evidence_summary: RACGP preventive guidance supports risk-targeted testing, not a universal pathology panel for asymptomatic adults by age alone. The lead-in list could imply a routine panel; reworded to foreground tailoring.
limitations: Lipids and diabetes-risk testing are broadly indicated in midlife; kidney/liver/iron studies are more selective. The retained 'not a set battery / knowing which tests you don't need' framing is the key protection.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 2 confirmed. RACGP Red Book URL verified live earlier this session.

claim_text: For most people in midlife, every one to two years is reasonable...
old_wording: For most people in midlife, every one to two years is reasonable, though it depends on your health and what we find.
new_wording: How often a review is useful depends on your age, your risk factors, your previous results and which screening is due, rather than a fixed schedule for everyone.

primary_source.title: Guidelines for preventive activities in general practice (Red Book)

evidence_summary: Preventive activities have their own risk-based intervals (e.g. CVD risk, screening cadences). There is no evidence base for a blanket 'comprehensive check every 1-2 years'. Reworded to risk-based framing.
limitations: None material after change.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 3 confirmed. MID agent (MID-19) flagged the same, noting the old wording survived only because it was conditioned on 'depends on your health'.

claim_text: the few actions that will make the most difference
old_wording: the few actions that will make the most difference
new_wording: the priorities most worth focusing on

primary_source.title: Guidelines for advertising a regulated health service

evidence_summary: 'Will make the most difference' is an outcome promise. Softened to a prioritisation statement, which preserves the marketing intent without implying a guaranteed result.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 4 confirmed.

claim_text: Continuity is linked to better health and fewer things falling through the cracks
old_wording: Continuity is linked to better health and fewer things falling through the cracks
new_wording: Continuity of care is linked to better patient experience and a range of better health outcomes

primary_source.title: Personal GP continuity improves healthcare outcomes in primary care populations: a systematic review

supporting_source.title: Continuity of care with doctors - a matter of life and death? A systematic review of continuity of care and mortality

evidence_summary: Systematic reviews associate higher GP continuity with reduced mortality, fewer hospital admissions and ED visits, better adherence and greater patient satisfaction. Evidence is observational (association, not proven causation). 'Better health' is well-supported; the vague 'fewer things falling through the cracks' was replaced with evidence-anchored 'better patient experience and a range of better health outcomes'.
limitations: Observational evidence - association, not established causation. Kept the wording associational ('linked to').
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 5 confirmed but note the evidence is stronger than the finding implied (includes mortality). GEN agent confirmed the continuity ARTICLE avoids a mortality claim; do not add one without observational-evidence qualification.

claim_text: Teenagers do better with a GP who takes them seriously and gives them room to speak for themselves.
old_wording: Teenagers do better with a GP who takes them seriously and gives them room to speak for themselves.
new_wording: Teenagers benefit from a GP who takes them seriously and gives them room to speak for themselves.

primary_source.title: Guidelines for preventive activities in general practice - adolescents (incl. psychosocial/HEEADSSS assessment)

evidence_summary: Adolescent-friendly, developmentally appropriate care (privacy, involving the young person) is a recognised care principle. 'Do better' framed a measurable outcome; reframed as a benefit/care principle.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 6 confirmed.

claim_text: starting sooner helps prevent scarring and the knock to confidence
old_wording: starting sooner helps prevent scarring and the knock to confidence
new_wording: starting sooner can reduce the risk of scarring and the impact on confidence, especially with moderate or severe acne

primary_source.title: Acne

evidence_summary: Early effective treatment reduces the RISK of scarring (particularly moderate/severe acne) rather than guaranteeing prevention; acne is associated with psychological impact. 'Prevent' softened to 'reduce the risk of', confidence reframed as 'impact on confidence'.
limitations: Scarring risk is greatest with inflammatory/moderate-severe acne; qualifier added.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 7 confirmed. Note the PILLAR agent considered the original 'safely hedged'; I adopted the more conservative independent-finding wording.

claim_text: Low iron (iron deficiency) is a common and very treatable cause of persistent tiredness
old_wording: Low iron (iron deficiency) is a common and very treatable cause of persistent tiredness
new_wording: Low iron (iron deficiency) is one of the more common and very treatable causes of persistent tiredness

primary_source.title: Iron deficiency

evidence_summary: Iron deficiency is genuinely common (esp. menstruating women) and very treatable, but fatigue has a wide differential. Minor softening to 'one of the more common' acknowledges the differential, which the surrounding sentence already lists (thyroid, sleep, mood, B12/D).
limitations: Fatigue differential is broad - the FAQ retains that context.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 8 confirmed as a minor, defensible softening.

claim_text: self-collection is now an option for most people
old_wording: self-collection is now an option for most people (FAQ + In brief)
new_wording: self-collection is now available to most people due for routine screening (some situations, such as certain symptoms or follow-up, still need a clinician-collected sample)

primary_source.org: National Cancer Screening Register / Dept of Health
primary_source.title: NCSP self-collection eligibility

evidence_summary: Self-collection (HPV test) is available to anyone eligible for routine cervical screening (25-74). Clinician collection is needed for co-test situations: symptoms suggestive of cervical cancer, test-of-cure follow-up, DES exposure, certain post-hysterectomy histories. 'For most people' is broadly right but the refined wording is more precise and safer.
limitations: Symptomatic patients need assessment, not routine screening - the refined wording flags this.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 9 confirmed. Verified this turn via NCSR + Cancer Council. WHS/PILLAR agents also confirmed 'for most people' was defensible; refined for precision.

claim_text: your baby is under 3 months old with any fever
old_wording: under 3 months old with any fever
new_wording: under 3 months old with a fever (a temperature of 38°C or higher)

primary_source.title: Clinical Practice Guideline: Febrile child / Fever in children

evidence_summary: Fever is defined as a temperature of 38°C or higher; a baby under 3 months with fever >=38°C needs urgent assessment. Adding the numeric threshold clarifies for parents without weakening the advice (below 38°C is not fever).
limitations: Does not weaken the red flag - it defines it. The immunisations article red-flag list was also split into 000 vs same-day tiers.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 10 confirmed. Note the PILLAR/CHILD agents judged 'any fever' deliberately safe; the numeric threshold adds precision consistent with RCH's definition of fever and was adopted.

claim_text: which usually involves referral to a paediatrician for formal assessment
old_wording: which usually involves referral to a paediatrician for formal assessment
new_wording: which may involve referral to a paediatrician, psychiatrist or another clinician experienced in ADHD assessment, depending on your child's needs and the local pathways

primary_source.title: Australian Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline for ADHD (NHMRC-approved)

evidence_summary: The NHMRC-approved Australian ADHD guideline supports multidisciplinary diagnosis (paediatricians, psychiatrists and other appropriately qualified clinicians), not paediatrician-only. Reworded to reflect this and jurisdictional/local pathway variation (e.g. emerging GP-led pathways).
limitations: Pathways vary by state/territory and clinician expertise; the new wording accommodates this.
reviewer_notes: Independent finding 11 confirmed. Verified this turn (AADPA guideline). PILLAR agent judged the original 'usually...paediatrician' acceptable; the revised multidisciplinary wording is more accurate and was adopted.

claim_text: Seek prompt care for fever, rapidly worsening redness, swelling, pus, honey-coloured crusting, painful skin, eczema around the eyes, widespread blisters or a child who seems very unwell.
old_wording: Seek prompt care for fever ... eczema around the eyes, widespread blisters or a child who seems very unwell.
new_wording: Separated bacterial skin infection (same-day) from eczema herpeticum (widespread/clustered blisters, eczema around the eyes = same-day herpes-infection assessment), and routed a very unwell child / non-blanching rash to 000.

primary_source.title: Kids Health Info / CPG: Eczema and eczema herpeticum

evidence_summary: Eczema herpeticum (widespread/clustered vesicles, peri-ocular involvement) needs same-day assessment; the original grouped it under generic 'prompt care', understating urgency.
limitations: None after change.
reviewer_notes: Sourced/verified by the CHILD audit agent (CHILD-11); implemented this turn.

claim_text: Seek urgent help if your child is at risk of harming themselves or others ... is expressing suicidal thoughts ...
old_wording: Seek urgent help if your child is at risk of harming themselves or others ... expressing suicidal thoughts ...
new_wording: call 000 or go to your nearest emergency department; also Kids Helpline 1800 55 1800 and Lifeline 13 11 14 (24 hours).

primary_source.title: Crisis support pathways

evidence_summary: Acute suicidality/harm risk needs an explicit emergency pathway; the single vague verb 'seek urgent help' was unsafe. Added 000/ED and crisis lines.
limitations: None after change.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (CHILD-05); implemented this turn.

claim_text: Seek urgent care for breathing difficulty, a baby under three months with fever ...
old_wording: Seek urgent care for breathing difficulty, a baby under three months with fever, ... a seizure, severe allergic reaction ...
new_wording: Split into Call 000 (breathing difficulty, seizure, severe allergic reaction, non-blanching rash, very drowsy/floppy/unrousable) vs same-day doctor (baby <3 months with fever 38°C+, dehydration, gut instinct).

primary_source.title: CPG: Febrile child; Anaphylaxis

evidence_summary: Emergency (000) and same-day tiers were merged under one verb; separated to match RCH urgency tiers, and added the 38°C threshold for <3-month fever.
limitations: None after change.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (CHILD-17) combined with independent finding 10; implemented this turn.

claim_text: Cervical screening is one of the most important preventive health checks for women and people with a cervix.
old_wording: Cervical screening is one of the most important preventive health checks for women and people with a cervix.
new_wording: Cervical screening is one of the most effective ways to help prevent cervical cancer for women and people with a cervix.

primary_source.title: Cervical cancer screening

evidence_summary: Ties the benefit to its mechanism (prevention of cervical cancer) and softens an unqualified superlative, consistent with AHPRA advertising guidance on superlatives.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (WHS-12); implemented this turn.

claim_text: Does PCOS mean I cannot get pregnant? No. Many individuals with this condition successfully conceive...
old_wording: No. Many individuals with this condition successfully conceive, sometimes supported by lifestyle modifications, cycle monitoring, medications or fertility interventions.
new_wording: No. PCOS is a common cause of reduced fertility, because ovulation can be irregular, but many people with PCOS do conceive - sometimes with lifestyle changes, cycle tracking, medications or fertility support.

primary_source.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)

evidence_summary: The reassurance is accurate but omitted that PCOS is a common cause of reduced fertility; the addition prevents the answer being read as 'PCOS does not affect fertility' (which could delay fertility assessment).
limitations: None after change.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (WHM-31); implemented this turn.

claim_text: pain that worsens over time (adenomyosis symptom list)
old_wording: pain that worsens over time
new_wording: pain that may worsen over time

primary_source.title: Adenomyosis

evidence_summary: Prognosis phrasing softened to match the article's otherwise hedged tone; not everyone experiences progressive pain.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Agent voice-consistency note (WHM-13); implemented this turn.

page_title: When should I see a GP before trying for a baby
claim_text: pregnancy vaccines that are recommended later in pregnancy, including influenza, pertussis, COVID-19, and RSV
old_wording: pregnancy vaccines that are recommended later in pregnancy, including influenza, pertussis, COVID-19, and RSV where relevant
new_wording: Some, such as whooping cough (pertussis) and RSV, are given at particular times later in pregnancy, while influenza and COVID-19 can be given at any stage.

primary_source.title: Vaccination for women who are pregnant

evidence_summary: Influenza and COVID-19 are recommended at any stage of pregnancy; pertussis (ideally ~20-32 weeks) and RSV (from 28 weeks) are timed later. Grouping all four under 'later in pregnancy' was imprecise and could prompt delay of flu/COVID vaccination.
limitations: Pregnancy vaccination guidance changes (RSV maternal vaccine added to the NIP in 2025) - short review cycle.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (PREG-30); implemented this turn.

claim_text: Hot flushes, sleep changes, mood and brain fog are common and treatable.
old_wording: Hot flushes, sleep changes, mood and brain fog are common and treatable.
new_wording: Hot flushes, sleep changes and mood changes are common and can often be helped, and many women also notice 'brain fog'.

primary_source.org: Jean Hailes for Women's Health / Australasian Menopause Society
primary_source.title: Menopause symptoms and management

evidence_summary: Vasomotor symptoms respond well to MHT; evidence that MHT treats cognitive 'brain fog' is weaker, so grouping brain fog under 'treatable' overstated certainty. Brain fog separated out as an experience.
limitations: MHT guidance is guideline-sensitive - short review cycle.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (PILLAR-13); implemented this turn.

claim_text: A GP is often the best place to start.
old_wording: A GP is often the best place to start.
new_wording: A GP is a good place to start.

primary_source.title: Guidelines for advertising a regulated health service

evidence_summary: 'Best' is comparative/superiority language cautioned against by AHPRA advertising guidance; softened to 'a good place to start'.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (PILLAR-13/14); implemented this turn.

claim_text: Most concerns can be assessed and managed in general practice.
old_wording: Most concerns can be assessed and managed in general practice, with referral arranged when it's needed.
new_wording: Many concerns can be assessed and managed in general practice, with referral arranged when it's needed.

primary_source.title: What is general practice / role of the GP

evidence_summary: 'Most' is an unsubstantiated quantified scope claim; softened to 'many' (also applied to the teenage 'handles most... from start to finish' -> 'can handle many').
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (PILLAR-18/34); both instances changed this turn.

claim_text: Often the reassurance is the treatment (puberty)
old_wording: Often the reassurance is the treatment, and knowing what to expect makes the rest easier.
new_wording: Often, once we've checked things over, the reassurance is the treatment, and knowing what to expect makes the rest easier.

primary_source.title: Adolescent health / clinical assessment

evidence_summary: Tied reassurance to prior clinical assessment so it doesn't read as reassuring symptoms away before they are checked.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (PILLAR-33); implemented this turn.

claim_text: so you know where your health stands and what to focus on next
old_wording: so you know where your health stands and what to focus on next
new_wording: to help you understand where your health stands and what to focus on next

primary_source.title: Guidelines for advertising a regulated health service

evidence_summary: Softened an implied certainty/completeness ('so you know') to 'to help you understand'.
limitations: None.
reviewer_notes: Agent finding (PILLAR-04); implemented this turn.

page_title: Credentials & affiliations (FRACGP, MBBS, AHPRA, Royal Hospital for Women shared care)
claim_text: Fellow of the RACGP (FRACGP), MBBS, registered medical practitioner (AHPRA), registered shared antenatal care provider - Royal Hospital for Women
old_wording: (unchanged)

primary_source.title: Practitioner registration lookup

evidence_summary: The RHW GP shared-care program exists and RACGP/AHPRA/MBBS are standard credentials, but THIS practitioner's current fellowship, registration and RHW shared-care affiliation cannot be verified from public sources. Must be substantiated by documentary evidence held by the practice, and kept current (RHW affiliation lapses each triennium without CPD).
limitations: Credential/affiliation accuracy is an AHPRA advertising and Australian Consumer Law requirement.
reviewer_notes: Flagged independently by WHS (Implanon/Mirena competency), PREG (RHW affiliation), MID (FRACGP), PILLAR (all credentials). ACTION FOR PRACTICE: confirm each against the AHPRA register and RHW accreditation and keep proof on file.

claim_text: Confidentiality / mature-minor / consent section ("What stays between the doctor and the patient")
old_wording: Prior 3-paragraph version: private one-to-one time; confidentiality with safety limits; capacity depends on understanding rather than a set age.
new_wording: Revised 2026-09-20 to a fuller 4-paragraph version: private one-to-one time as routine adolescent care; confidentiality with explicit limits incl. serious harm/safety and disclosure required or permitted by law; mature-minor / Gillick competence assessed per specific healthcare decision (understanding of purpose, risks, benefits, alternatives, consequences); parent/guardian consent where the young person lacks capacity; encourage appropriate family involvement where helpful and the young person is comfortable.

primary_source.title: Consent to Medical and Healthcare Treatment Manual (mature minor)

supporting_source.title: Confidentiality and consent in adolescent health

evidence_summary: Aligns with the NSW mature-minor / Gillick approach and confidentiality-with-limits. The revised wording is more precise and legally framed than the prior version.
limitations: Consent/confidentiality law is jurisdiction-specific and consequential.
reviewer_notes: Wording revised 2026-09-20 and supersedes the PILLAR-29/30 FAQ restatements (removed). Signed off by the practice medical defence organisation 2026-09-20 - approved for use as written. No fixed consent age asserted; mature-minor/Gillick approach assessed per decision.

page_title: Independent findings assessed as already-adequate (no change)
claim_text: Menopause/MHT individualisation; cervical screening ages 25-74 & 5-yearly & HPV-vaccine-does-not-replace-screening; starting solids ~6 months / not before 4 / allergens in first year; ADHD article differential; pregnancy medication/vaccine caution
old_wording: (unchanged)

primary_source.org: Multiple (ASCIA, NCSP, Jean Hailes/AMS, AADPA, Australian Immunisation Handbook)
primary_source.title: See per-domain fragments (WHM, WHS, CHILD, PREG)

evidence_summary: The independent review's 'strong areas' were independently confirmed by the domain agents and retained without change. ASCIA infant-feeding guidance confirmed updated Jan 2026 and the site's ~6-months / not-before-4 / allergens-in-first-year wording matches it.
limitations: Guidance-sensitive - carried with review dates (see per-domain fragments).
reviewer_notes: Confirms the user's 'areas considered strong'. No rewriting done, per instruction not to sanitise accurate content.
